messages:
marta: Thinking about auto-mapping runtime errors -> degrade modes. Short sketch: map 5xx spikes to "soft_degrade" (lower quality model), rate-limit errors -> "throttled_degrade" (queue + 429 fallback), and memory OOMs -> "hard_degrade" (circuit to cached response). wanting UX input on how to present this in console and what operator affordances we need.

 tom: +1. Where does the mapping live? Per-route policy or global?

 marta: plan is per-route with inherited defaults. console shows route-level override list and a preview simulator. but questions: how detailed should the error -> mode mapping be? raw error codes, error categories, or heuristics (latency spike + p50 jump)?

 anna (Platform PM): Operators want simple controls. I'd bias towards categories + a single "advanced" toggle for raw-code rules. show human-readable explanation like: "If 5xx rate > 2% in 5m -> switch to soft_degrade". Also need audit trail: who changed rule, why, and the simulated impact.

 liam: For API shape I propose a compact rule schema we can surface in UI. Example: 
```json
{
  "rule_id": "r-01",
  "scope": "route:/chat/completion",
  "trigger": { "type": "error_category", "value": "server_error", "threshold": 0.02, "window_s": 300 },
  "action": { "degrade_mode": "soft_degrade", "fallback_model": "gptx-small-q8", "sample_audit": 0.01 }
}
```
Notes: sample_audit is fraction of requests stored for audit when degraded. keep payload tiny for fast evaluation and console preview.

 marta: like this. two UX asks: (1) in console preview, show expected latency/cost delta and % of requests that will be audited. (2) for operators, provide an immediate "dry-run" toggle that logs decisions without switching traffic.

 tom: Implementation note: dry-run should surface a live count and recent examples in the preview panel. But we need limits on retained samples so we don't blow storage — tie to quota. Also: who can flip a rule? RBAC needed (ops vs. eng).

 anna (Platform PM): Agree on RBAC and audit. Also want an automatic revert option: if degraded for > X minutes with no improvement, revert to previous state and notify. That'll stop bad handoffs.

 liam: We can emit a compact audit event when a request is routed to a degrade path: 
```json
{ "ts":"...","route":"/chat/completion","rule_id":"r-01","decision":"soft_degrade","reason":"5xx_rate>0.02","model": "gptx-small-q8","sampled": true }
```
These should land in the same audit index as rollouts/changes so forensic joins are easy. Sampled events only for sample_audit fraction + deterministic hashing for reproducibility.

 marta: UX: when showing an example of a degraded request in the console, redact PII and highlight what changed (model, temperature, truncation). Also clearly show fallback provenance (why this model was chosen).

 tom: edge case: transient noise — we should add hysteresis (min duration before flip) and cooldown after revert. UI should allow editing those knobs but default conservatively.

 anna (Platform PM): good. Action items: 1) liam: draft API schema + audit event spec. 2) marta: mock console flows (preview + dry-run + revert UI) 3) tom: design quota + retention guardrails for sampled audits 4) i'll write RBAC and revert policy defaults.

 ops-bot: Deploy-check: no blocking config conflicts found for route:/chat/completion. CI lint OK.

 liam: will post a first-pass spec by EOD. I'll include examples for rate-based, latency-based, and error-code rules.

 marta: thanks — want a short UX sync tomorrow 10am to walk mockups.

 anna (Platform PM): 10am works. tagging @ops for awareness after spec lands. :sparkles:
